title: Metric gaps and alert tuning scratchpad
content:
TL;DR: During a set of SLO burn alerts last week we saw repeated short-duration metric gaps and large SLO delta spikes tied to two distinct failure modes: (1) exporter memory-pressure causing intermittent scrape failures (5–90s gaps), and (2) rollouts of the autoscaler that removed pods faster than the service discovery TTLs updated, producing stale targets and backfilled zeros in aggregated queries. These produced noisy SLO burn alerts and pager churn. This doc captures hypotheses, quick mitigation steps for on-call, experimental checks to validate the root cause, and longer-term tuning proposals.

Observed symptoms (from alert runbooks + traces):
- Multiple SLO burn events between 2026-02-18 02:30–06:45 UTC where 50th->95th latency percentiles jumped then returned within 2–5 minutes.
- Prometheus scrape logs show repeated 503/connection reset errors against exporter pods coinciding with metric gaps.
- Aggregated metrics (service_request_latency_seconds_bucket) showed sudden collapse to fewer series which made histograms compute incorrect percentiles temporarily.
- During a peak autoscaler activity window there were 20–30s intervals where targets returned 404 in service discovery before being removed, causing high-cardinality queries to read partial shards.
- Alerts triggered: SLO-burn-high (5m window), p99-latency-spike, request-success-rate-drop. Many were resolved automatically when scrapes resumed.

Immediate on-call checklist (fast actions to stabilize):
1) Confirm alert context and affected customers: open incident ticket and annotate which customer SLOs are impacted.
2) Check prometheus scrape status: Grafana panel -> Prometheus > Status > Targets. If exporters in unknown/down state, note last scrape times.
3) If exporter pods show OOMKilled or high memory RSS in metrics -> scale replica counts up by +1 and temporarily increase memory request (via patch) if safe.
4) If scrape failures line up with autoscaler rollouts, temporarily set autoscaler to more conservative scale-down-delay (example: horizontal-pod-autoscaler.spec.behaviour.scaleDown.stabilizationWindowSeconds = 300) for the affected deployment.
5) Silence SLO-burn alerts if the incident is already being mitigated and noise is causing further churn. Add a short rationale to the alert silence message.
6) If there's an immediate customer-impacting outage, failover to the compatible model variant / region per the fallback policy.

Hypotheses and validation queries (fast tests):
- Hypothesis A: exporter memory pressure -> intermittent 5–90s scrape failures.
  * Validate: check kube events and container OOM events for exporter namespace around the times. Example kubectl: kubectl -n monitoring get events --sort-by=.lastTimestamp --field-selector involvedObject.name=<exporter-pod-name>
  * PromQL sanity checks: (a) rate(process_virtual_memory_bytes_total[5m])? (b) increase(prometheus_scrape_duration_seconds_count[15m]) by (instance)
  * Quick grafana: panel showing prometheus_target_interval_length_seconds and prometheus_target_scrape_pool_timestamp_seconds for the exporter pool.

- Hypothesis B: service-discovery lag on scale-down -> stale targets and partial aggregation zeros.
  * Validate: compare kube endpoints list vs prometheus SD: curl to the prometheus /api/v1/targets and parse lastScrape and lastError fields for endpoints that later disappear.
  * PromQL check: count(up{job="service-x"}) by (instance) over time; sudden drops to fractional counts indicate partial sharding.

Data artifacts to collect for post-incident analysis:
- Prometheus /targets json dump for the 2 hour window around incidents.
- Exporter pod logs (stderr/stdout) for the same window and kube events.
- Alert manager history and silence events.
- Deployment rollout timings (kubectl rollout history and HPA events).
- Raw histogram buckets for the service_request_latency_seconds histogram (snapshot before/during/after event).

Runbook adjustments proposed (short-term):
- Add a synthetic heartbeat metric for each exporter: exporter_heartbeat{instance} with a 60s TTL. Alert if heartbeat missing for >2 scrape intervals.
- Lower alert sensitivity for SLO-burn-high: change evaluation window from 5m to 10m for team-internal SLOs to reduce transient flapping; keep customer-facing SLOs strict.
- For histograms: switch queries to use quantile_over_time(histogram_quantile(0.95, sum(rate(...[5m])) by (le))) with a smoothing window in the alerting rule to avoid single-bucket drops causing large p95 swings.
- For autoscaler churn: add a small delay in SD refresh via relabeling or set pod readiness gate so pods stay discoverable for a few seconds after termination signal.

Longer-term mitigations (owner + timeline):
- Owner: Lina Chen. Task: add exporter heartbeat + dashboard and alerting rule. ETA: 2 sprint cycles.
- Owner: Rajiv Menon. Task: add resource-guard (memory lim/requests review) and HPA scale-down stabilization. ETA: next on-call rotation.
- Owner: SRE tooling. Task: implement a quick-check service that compares kube endpoints vs Prometheus SD every minute and emits a 'sd_discrepancy' metric. ETA: prototype in 3 weeks.
- Owner: Product infra. Task: review histogram bucket alignment and recommend safe query patterns and pre-aggregation channels for high-cardinality tables. ETA: 1 month.

Experiment plan (A/B testing changes):
- Experiment 1: add heartbeat metric and a firing rule that needs 2 consecutive missing checks (2m) before page. Measure pager count delta over 2 weeks.
- Experiment 2: change SLO alert window to 10m for internal SLOs and observe number of pages vs customer-facing incidents over 30 days.
- Experiment 3: temporarily increase exporter memory requests by 30% in a single cluster pool to validate if scrape failures disappear; run under traffic capture and monitor OOM events.

Example PromQL snippets to include in dashboards / rules: 
- Scrape health by instance: up{job="exporter-service"}
- Scrape latency variance: histogram_quantile(0.99, sum(rate(prometheus_scrape_duration_seconds_bucket[5m])) by (le))
- SD drift detection: count(up{job="service-x"}) - count(kube_endpoint_address_available{endpoint="service-x"})
- Heartbeat rule: absent(up{job="exporter-service", heartbeat="1"})

Postmortem quick notes (to include in the official incident review):
- Root causes: exporter memory pressure + aggressive autoscaler scale-down.
- Why alerts fired: aggregation windows and histogram queries amplify short gaps into large percentile deviations.
- What worked: quick scale-up of exporter replicas and setting temporary silence on SLO-burn reduced pager churn.
- What needs follow-up: implement heartbeats, SD discrepancy metric, HPA stabilization, and dashboarding of histogram bucket health.

Open action items (tracking):
- SRE-Action-001: add exporter heartbeat and rule (owner: Lina Chen, ETA: 2026-03-15)
- SRE-Action-002: change internal SLO evaluation window to 10m (owner: Asha Patel, ETA: 2026-03-05)
- SRE-Action-003: prototype SD discrepancy checker (owner: SRE tooling, ETA: 2026-03-22)
- SRE-Action-004: run exporter mem request increase in staging and monitor (owner: Rajiv Menon, ETA: 2026-03-01)

Notes to self / loose thoughts:
- Consider adding a 'partial-aggregation' label to alerts when count(up) < expected replica count so we can silence percentile-based alerts automatically.
- Investigate whether the histogram bucketing is too fine-grained for our aggregated queries; coarse buckets may be more stable for alerting.
- Document the tradeoffs of increasing scrape interval (cost savings) vs increased detection latency. For low-traffic endpoints maybe 30s -> 60s is fine.

Slack channels and people to ping during the next incident: #sre-oncall, #infra-exporters, @Lina.Chen, @Rajiv.Menon, @eng-observability.

This is a working scratchpad. Will extract a clean runbook and follow-up Jira tasks after validating experiments and collecting artifacts.
